text: Team lead purchasing $750 USD in cloud testing credits (Tier 1) with written approval from Direct Manager.
gold_policy_passage: Tier 1 (Up to $1,000 USD): Requires Direct Manager approval.

text: Engineering manager purchasing $6,000 USD dev tooling license (Tier 2) with approvals from Direct Manager and Department Director.
gold_policy_passage: Tier 2 ($1,001 to $10,000 USD): Requires Direct Manager and Department Head (Director) approval.

text: Project manager initiating a $7,500 USD software procurement with only Direct Manager sign-off, missing Department Director approval.
gold_policy_passage: Tier 2 ($1,001 to $10,000 USD): Requires Direct Manager and Department Head (Director) approval.

text: Department purchasing enterprise infrastructure worth $65,000 USD with CFO and CEO signatures and 3 competitive vendor bids.
gold_policy_passage: Tier 4 (Over $50,000 USD): Requires Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) sign-off, alongside competitive bidding documentation (minimum 3 vendor quotes).

text: Manager attempting to purchase $70,000 enterprise software contract without obtaining 3 vendor quotes (only 1 quote provided).
gold_policy_passage: Tier 4 (Over $50,000 USD): Requires Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) sign-off, alongside competitive bidding documentation (minimum 3 vendor quotes).

text: Procurement officer deliberately splitting a single $18,000 vendor contract into two $9,000 purchase orders to avoid Tier 3 Controller sign-off.
gold_policy_passage: Intentionally splitting a single procurement order, software license batch, or service invoice into multiple smaller invoices to circumvent approval limits is strictly prohibited.

text: Employee using corporate P-Card to purchase monthly AWS cloud hosting charges ($120 USD) with itemized receipt submitted in 3 days.
gold_policy_passage: Corporate P-Cards are issued solely for legitimate, pre-approved business operations, SaaS subscription renewals, emergency field supplies, and authorized business travel.

text: Employee using corporate P-Card to buy personal cryptocurrency and luxury resort tickets.
gold_policy_passage: P-Cards must never be used for personal expenses, personal cash advances, gambling, cryptocurrency transactions, or luxury/spa services.

text: Employee with unreconciled P-Card transaction of $200 USD remaining unsubmitted for 38 calendar days.
gold_policy_passage: If an employee fails to submit receipts within 30 calendar days, the card will be suspended, and non-reconciled balances may be deducted from payroll.

text: Employee submitting P-Card charge of $55 USD on day 4 without attaching an itemized tax receipt.
gold_policy_passage: Transactions exceeding $25 USD require an itemized digital tax invoice.

text: Accounts payable issuing $20,000 initial payment to a new offshore vendor who has completed KYV tax verification and sanctions screening.
gold_policy_passage: All new commercial vendors, contractors, and service providers must complete vendor risk assessment (KYV), tax registration verification, and sanctions screening prior to initial invoice payment.

text: Project lead requesting immediate wire transfer of $15,000 to a newly created consulting firm without completing KYV or sanctions clearance.
gold_policy_passage: All new commercial vendors, contractors, and service providers must complete vendor risk assessment (KYV), tax registration verification, and sanctions screening prior to contract execution or initial invoice payment.

text: Vendor demanding a 60% upfront advance payment ($30,000 USD) on a custom consulting engagement without providing a performance bank guarantee.
gold_policy_passage: Advance payments to suppliers exceeding 30% of total contract value are prohibited unless backed by a performance bank guarantee or approved by the Finance Controller.

text: Account executive hosting prospective client dinner for 4 attendees at $85 USD per attendee ($340 total) with attendee names and business agenda attached.
gold_policy_passage: Business meals hosted for prospective or active clients are reimbursable up to $100 USD per attendee. Itemized dining receipts must list the names, affiliations, and business purpose.

text: Sales director claiming $160 USD per attendee for a lavish 2-person dinner with prospective clients.
gold_policy_passage: Business meals hosted for prospective or active clients are reimbursable up to $100 USD per attendee (including taxes and gratuity).

text: Client appreciation banquet totaling $1,400 USD submitted without prior written Department VP authorization.
gold_policy_passage: Total entertainment spend exceeding $1,000 USD for a single event requires advance written authorization from the Department Vice President.

text: Engineering team hosting quarterly celebration for 10 members at $35 USD per person ($350 total) with manager approval.
gold_policy_passage: Quarterly departmental team dinners or morale events are budgeted at a ceiling of $40 USD per employee.

text: Employee buying a $2,200 MacBook Pro directly on personal credit card and submitting an expense reimbursement claim.
gold_policy_passage: All laptops, monitors, servers, and telecommunication hardware must be procured exclusively via Centralized IT Procurement. Individual employee purchases of computing devices via expense reimbursement are strictly prohibited.

text: Employee used corporate P-Card to buy cryptocurrency.
gold_policy_passage: Corporate P-Cards must never be used for personal expenses, cash advances, cryptocurrency, gambling, or luxury services.

text: Team lead purchasing a $1,500 USD software license without Director approval.
gold_policy_passage: Tier 2 purchase ($1,500.0) requires approvals from both Direct Manager and Department Head (Director).

text: Employee purchasing a laptop via reimbursement.
gold_policy_passage: Hardware and computing devices must be procured exclusively via Centralized IT Procurement, not employee reimbursement.

text: Vendor onboarding with a 40% advance payment and no bank guarantee.
gold_policy_passage: Advance supplier payments exceeding 30% are prohibited without a performance bank guarantee.

text: Client dinner costing $120 USD per person.
gold_policy_passage: Client dining expense exceeds the maximum limit of $100 USD per attendee.

text: P-Card reconciliation overdue by 35 days.
gold_policy_passage: P-Card reconciliation overdue (35 days); unreconciled balances beyond 30 days trigger card suspension and payroll deduction.

text: Procurement of $60,000 USD software with only 2 vendor quotes.
gold_policy_passage: Procurements exceeding $50,000 require minimum 3 competitive vendor quotes.

text: Team dinner costing $50 USD per person.
gold_policy_passage: Internal team dinner cost exceeds the $40 USD per employee ceiling.

text: Tier 3 purchase of $20,000 without Finance Controller approval.
gold_policy_passage: Tier 3 purchase requires approvals from Department Head, Procurement Lead, and Finance Controller.

text: New vendor onboarding approved by Legal but missing KYV screening.
gold_policy_passage: Emergency vendor onboarding without standard KYV screening authorized via Legal & Compliance override.

text: Client event costing $1,500 USD total without VP pre-approval.
gold_policy_passage: Single client entertainment event exceeding $1,000 USD requires advance Department VP written authorization.

text: Tier 1 purchase of $500 USD with manager approval.
gold_policy_passage: Tier 1 purchase within $1,000 threshold with manager approval.
